subject: Hosted → Dedicated migration: financing safety-net, throughput guarantees, and bridge months
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <obarnes@quantumpay.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: QuantumPay Procurement <procure@quantumpay.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted → Dedicated migration: initial ask and usage context

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. We ran the internal sizing exercise and wanted to put some concrete asks on the table as we evaluate a move from Redwood hosted API to Dedicated capacity. High level: we need predictable unit economics for Q3, a throughput SLA for our high-concurrency checkout flows, and a clean conversion for the credits we've accrued on hosted spend.

Quick context: our hosted spend has averaged ~$210k/month over the last 3 months (mostly generation + embeddings for search/rerank). Peak concurrency during US peak window is ~120 concurrent streams, avg response sizes ~120 tokens. We expect ~2x growth over the next 6 months.

Questions we need answered to take this to procurement:
- How do you propose converting hosted credits to reserved commit offsets? (formula and timing)
- Can we get a short-term safety-net (bridge months) if committed capacity lags our growth?
- What throughput guarantees do you commit to (tokens/sec or concurrency) per GPU pool, and how are penalties handled?
- Example commit sizing & expected monthly cost for an 8–12 GPU pool (A100/80GB equiv).

We can share the raw telemetry if that helps — attaching the condensed usage report and a worksheet with our forecast. Looking to get something draft by end of next week so procurement can decide whether to include this in their May run.

Attachments: Hosted_usage_summary_QP_Apr2027.csv; Dedicated_Sizing_Worksheet.xlsx

Olivia Barnes
Head of Platform Engineering, QuantumPay
obarnes@quantumpay.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <obarnes@quantumpay.com>

Date: 2027-04-19T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted → Dedicated migration: initial ask and usage context

Hi Olivia — great detail, thanks. I skimmed the worksheet and the hosted spend numbers make the migration case clear. Below is a pragmatic starting proposal we can put in a short MOU for procurement while our legal & finance teams work the contract redlines. I put the high-level items first and then the mechanics.

1) Conversion credits (hosted → commit offsets)
- Proposal: convert 6 months of average hosted spend into an up-front offset applied to the first 6 months of the Dedicated commit. Example: if hosted avg = $210k/mo, conversion credit = 30% of that amount applied monthly against committed invoice for 6 months. (This equates to a temporary effective discount while you ramp onto reserved capacity.)

2) Bridge months / safety-net
- Proposal: two bridge months where overflow capacity beyond the committed pool is served by our hosted fleet at a 60% discount off standard hosted list rates (to avoid availability gaps while Dedicated autoscaling finalizes). After bridge months, overflow will be billed at normal hosted rates unless we agree a longer ramp.

3) Throughput & latency guarantees
- Target: maintain 99.5% of requests below 350ms for 0–128 token generations within the committed GPU pool under the agreed concurrency profile.
- Throughput measurement: tokens/sec averaged over 5-minute windows across the pool; we'll define traffic routing rules in the MOU (priority routing for checkout flows).
- Penalty: credits applied to the following month (pro-rated) if SLA not met more than two times in a rolling 90-day window.

4) Sizing example (ballpark)
- 8x A100-80GB equiv pool: target sustained throughput ~12k tokens/sec aggregate; expect to handle ~120–150 concurrent streams at median latency targets above.
- 12x pool: ~18k tokens/sec, better headroom for 2x growth.
- We'll validate with your telemetry and the attached sizing worksheet; results may nudge the GPU sku / count.

5) Contractual asks from Redwood
- Minimum 12-month committed term for the reserved pricing to apply.
- Commitment billing monthly with ability to true-up at quarter boundaries based on usage signals.

Next steps: I'll run the numbers with Finance and Rishi on our side to confirm the conversion credit percent and exact SLA language, then share an MOU + draft SLA PDF you can circulate. Are you available for a 30-min sync on Wednesday to finalize the MOU framing?

Attachments: Dedicated_Sizing_Worksheet.xlsx (we updated a few sizing heuristics)

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

— Alex

Alex — thanks for the context. Quick internal position from finance & product:

1) Conversion credit — scale back to 25% of avg hosted for the first 6 months (vs 30%). We can do 30% for a heavier commit (>= 18 months) but for a 12-month minimum 25% is the safer baseline. The conversion credit should be amortized monthly against the committed invoice rather than an upfront lump credit (helps our billing cadence).

2) Bridge months — okay to offer two bridge months at 60% off hosted list, but add a cap on total bridge-hosted volume per month (e.g., no more than 150% of current baseline) to avoid open-ended exposure. After bridge months, overflow will be billed at normal hosted rates unless we agree a staged scale policy.

3) SLA & throughput guarantees — product input: define throughput as tokens/sec across the committed pool, measured in 5-minute rolling windows. We can offer a 99.5% latency SLA for the agreed size profile. If SLA misses accrue, apply a service credit equal to 1% of monthly committed invoice per SLA miss after the second miss in a 90-day period, up to 10% of invoice that month.

4) Minimums & financial protection — require a 12-month minimum commit and a one-month notice for reductions at quarter boundaries. Also propose a quarterly usage review to allow right-sizing (and potential modest true-up credits).

5) Approvals & docs — I'll draft the amortization schedule and sample invoice language. Can you confirm the pool SKU assumptions (A100 equiv) and whether QuantumPay expects preemption-tolerant jobs on the same pool? If so we need to size for reserved preemption headroom.

I think we can accept the rest, but we should avoid open-ended hosted exposure. If Alex is comfortable with 25% conversion credit & caps on bridge volume, I'll push this to legal/finance for the MOU text.

Rishi
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
